Henry Morton Stanley 
Berlin Conference 
Topic: Imperial Interests 
 
​
The Berlin conference was a crucial part of modern history and forever changed the 
political atmosphere of the time as well as the future of Africa as a whole. While most of the 
actual carving of african borders didn't happen until later years the berlin conference set the 
standard for the colonization of africa. Among many things such as the drawing the borders of 
belgian congo and the passing of the General act another crucial agreement was made “The 
Principle of effective occupation” allowing any power the right to colonial land so long as they 
were capable of governing the land meaning any colonial claim was openly recognized by all 
colonial nations. This led to a wave of african colonization known as the african scramble that 
eventually led to the almost complete annexation of africa to colonial powers. 
​
Previous to the Berlin conference there was 1 major agreement named the anglo-french 
agreement this agreement settled a colonial dispute between the britain and france regarding 
conflicting african territory. The outcome of this agreement had both sides recognize each other's 
colonial territories as well as their respective spheres of influence; this resulted in neither nation 
getting in each other's way in regards to colonial expansion. This agreement was a success with 
no colonial wars between the two nations.  
​
I, Henry Morton Stanley, am a British-American Explorer, Journalist and soldier. Despite 
not being a Belgian myself I represent the Belgian claims on the Congo after failing to gain 
British interest in the region. Belgium seeks that the berlin conference recognize their claim to 
the “Congo free state” These claims would allow the uncontested colonization of the region 
which the belgians sought for its rich resources and large populations. Before the conference I 
had charted trade routes and created claims within the Congo for Belgium. I am against the slave 
trade for acts I had Witnessed caused by the slave trade. I seek that the Congo is recognized by 
the committee as the rightful and legal territory of the Belgian Government and that any and all 
claims of the land are recognized. I also seek the abolition of slavery and the transatlantic slave 
trade.
